thread:
jamie: Heads up — customer alerted that allocation totals in the Rollout Insights page are wrong for experiment `new-tokenizer-v2`. UI shows a 60/40 split but the raw assignment logs are ~40/60. They flagged billing impact. :eyes:
kevin: Can you attach a screenshot and an export of the assignment rows? which environment (prod/dedicated)?
jamie: Prod. Screenshot: <https://redwood.s3/exp-screens/1876543210.png>. Quick repro I ran in console export: `GET /api/experiments/new-tokenizer-v2/assignments?start=2026-03-10&end=2026-03-16` returned CSV with these lines:
```
user_id,variant,assigned_at
u1001,treatment,2026-03-12T23:58:12Z
u1002,control,2026-03-12T23:58:54Z
u1003,treatment,2026-03-13T00:01:04Z
u1004,control,2026-03-13T00:02:11Z
```
But the dashboard daily totals for 2026-03-13 show 800 treatment / 1200 control, while raw event counts are 1200 treatment / 800 control.
anya: Is the mismatch only in the aggregated totals (daily/hourly) or also in the per-request assignment audit logs?
jamie: Audit logs match raw events (we pulled from assignments.events table). The mismatch appears when viewing "Traffic split (by day)" and the heatmap in Rollout Insights. Screenshot shows legend colors swapped vs numbers.
kevin: Two quick hypotheses: 1) rollup job uses local tz cut (server at UTC+1) and misassigns a few hours to the previous day; 2) label mapping bug when rendering the legend (control/treatment label swap). Can you run this quick SQL to confirm raw vs rollup counts?
```
-- raw events
SELECT variant, count(*) FROM assignments.events
WHERE experiment = 'new-tokenizer-v2' AND assigned_at >= '2026-03-10' AND assigned_at < '2026-03-17'
GROUP BY variant;
-- rollup table
SELECT day, variant, assigned_total FROM experiments.daily_rollups
WHERE experiment = 'new-tokenizer-v2' AND day BETWEEN '2026-03-10' AND '2026-03-16';
```
jamie: Ran it — raw shows treatment 12,345 / control 8,210. daily_rollups show the opposite.
luis: If labels are swapped in the rendering layer that would explain swapped totals without touching the rollup DB. But since rollups are also reversed, sounds like transformation in the aggregation pipeline could be flipping the variant key during map/reduce. Any recent deploys to the rollup lambda?
support-bot: Created ticket SUP-4187 (priority P1) — data-team + product on the thread.
kevin: I checked last deploys: rollup-worker v2.7.1 rolled at 2026-03-12 23:50 UTC (deploy log ID: deploy-9876). The worker change replaced a hash map and there was a rename from `variant_key` -> `group_key`. Patch likely mis-merged. I'm running a local replay of events through v2.6.9 vs v2.7.1 to diff outputs. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
olivia: Billing flagged this as potential overcharge for one enterprise customer. We'll pause auto-invoicing for that account and hold any usage dispute until we have root cause. Please add an ETA.
kevin: Quick mitigation: add a temporary check in Rollout Insights UI to compute totals from raw events API instead of relying on daily_rollups for the affected experiment(s). Patch branch: `hotfix/insights-verify-rollups` — pushing to staging now.
deploy-bot: Started deploy of `hotfix/insights-verify-rollups` to staging (staging-456).
anya: Also adding a one-off reconciliation job to recompute daily_rollups for 2026-03-10..2026-03-16 using v2.6.9 aggregator. If confirmed, we'll backfill prod and mark the bad rollup runs as invalid.
luis: Product note — we'll show a banner on Rollout Insights for experiments that were processed by rollup-worker v2.7.1 until reconciliation completes. Keeps customers notified.
jamie: Thanks — I've told the customer we're investigating and held billing. Please post ETA here when you have it. :thumbsup:
kevin: Initial diff shows a deterministic flip in map step; ETA for fix + prod backfill: ~6 hours once we get approval to run backfill (data size ~80M rows). Will update SUP-4187.
olivia: Holding invoices; will escalate if ETA > 8h.
jamie: Appreciated. I'll keep customer updated and will paste any extra logs they send.
kevin: Final note: if anyone needs a repro, use `assignment_log` export for the date range and compare to UI. That'll be our ground truth until rollups are repaired.
jamie: OK — standing by. Thanks everyone.
